ledger.note: Searched the sheet's existing refs and the EIA entries, then one search on Eastern Shore and LNG. A June 2006 NGI article says the Eastern Shore company planned a 60,000 Dth/d expansion that would carry gas from the Cove Point LNG terminal under Chesapeake Bay to Delmarva. That tie belongs to the expansion, not this main line, and it is not a row in this chunk, so nothing is staged on the main line.

Searched for the Ehrenberg to San Luis Rio Colorado line and LNG. The only sources describe a Mexico gas line for power and the line is listed as cancelled. No LNG tie was found, so nothing is staged.
Checked the EIA entries and the existing refs. The El Paso system is a whole-system row that serves Mexico and western power markets. No source ties it to LNG, so nothing is staged.

Checked the EIA entry, which says the Carlsbad South project adds Permian takeaway capacity to a compressor station and the Keystone pool. It does not mention LNG, and one search found no LNG tie, so nothing is staged.
Searched the Willcox Lateral and LNG. The sources describe a line that serves power plants and a copper mine in Sonora, Mexico. No LNG tie was found, so nothing is staged.
Checked the EIA entries and the existing refs for the Empire main line. Empire serves New York and Pennsylvania markets and connects to Ontario. No source ties it to LNG, so nothing is staged.
Checked the EIA entries and the existing refs for the Empire North expansion. The sources describe a link to Ontario and New York markets. No source ties it to LNG, so nothing is staged.
Checked the EIA entry and the Federal Register notice on the Tuscarora Lateral. The lateral serves New York markets. No LNG tie was found, so nothing is staged.

Searched for the Carthage to Perryville line and LNG. Federal and trade press sources describe expansions driven by Haynesville shale takeaway. One older proposal by a different company mentioned LNG volumes, but it is a separate line. No LNG tie for this line was found, so nothing is staged.
Checked the EIA entry and the Federal Register notices for the Childes lateral. It was built for a gas storage expansion in Oklahoma. No LNG tie was found, so nothing is staged.
Checked the EIA entry for the MASS expansion. It adds takeaway capacity out of the Anadarko basin. The tracker's sources do not tie it to LNG, and one search found no LNG tie, so nothing is staged.

Searched the Enable system and LNG. The LNG link found is the Gulf Run project, which would carry gas to Golden Pass LNG. That is a separate project with its own route, and the sources do not say this main line delivers gas to a terminal. Nothing is staged on the main line.
Checked the EIA entry and the Federal Register notice for the Tontitown project in Arkansas. No LNG tie was found, so nothing is staged.

Searched Enable Oklahoma Intrastate Transmission and LNG. The sources describe an in-state system that connects to interstate lines. The LNG link found is the Gulf Run project on the interstate system, not this line. Nothing is staged.
Searched the Transok West-to-East expansion and LNG. The EIA entry and search results show an Oklahoma line from 1997 with no LNG tie, so nothing is staged.

Searched the Enterprise Wilson storage link and LNG. The sources describe a 2012 residue gas line from a processing plant to a storage site in Texas. Enterprise's LNG-linked lines are other projects. No LNG tie for this line was found, so nothing is staged.
Searched the Equitrans Mainline and LNG. The sources describe Appalachian takeaway and Mountain Valley links, with no LNG tie for the mainline, so nothing is staged.
Checked the EIA entries and the Federal Register notice for the Sunrise project. The line moves Marcellus gas to Pennsylvania and West Virginia markets. No LNG tie was found, so nothing is staged.

Checked the EIA entry for the AE Cooperative Upgrade in Mississippi and Alabama, built in 2001. The separate FGT East-West project serves Gulf Coast LNG, but it is not this row. No LNG tie was found for this upgrade, so nothing is staged.
Checked the EIA entry for the Alabama Power Lateral, built in 1998. It serves a power plant in Alabama. No LNG tie was found, so nothing is staged.
